what_it_did.what_the_split_means: A mechanical commit republishes an unchanged net -- the report, the dashboard, the state files. Counting those as work would make a quiet day look busy, so they are separated rather than filtered: they happened, they are just not progress.

what_it_decided.thesis_read: Three hours, six commits, two substantive, and both of the substantive ones are measurements that came back NO -- which is the best thing that happened, and it still leaves the thesis further away than the headline says. The important one is item two, which landed in full and can leave this file: the realised A/B comparison CANNOT separate "the company inferred well" from "the world does not punish price". Effective n is 4, not 42 -- 18 of the 42 priced renewals are unpunishable at any multiplier because the world rolled no decision for them, and the roster diff is 3 in, 1 out. It also found WHY the two sides disagree without either lying: the company keys churn on a DELTA against its own prior rate, the world keys on a LEVEL against SVT, so cheap-to-average reads as a big rise and lands at parity while dear-and-flat reads as flat and lands +30% vs SVT. That is the observed inversion on both tails, and it means the +GBP 16,773 headline is neither refuted nor confirmed -- the instrument that was supposed to attribute it is under-powered by construction, and no number of re-runs fixes that. EP13 also produced real science and also came back negative: pinning biomass to its metered outturn -- perfect knowledge, deliberately unpublishable, structurally proven unable to reach the feed -- moves correlation the WRONG way in four years of six, mean -0.0050, so the outage model is retired as the next gap and the reason generalises (70-86% of that fleet's variance is between days, and within-day is the axis holding the level). But it is not what I asked EP13 for. There is still no `tools/couple_carbon_intensity.py` among the fifteen `couple_*.py`, still no EP13 row among the sixteen in `coupled_gap_ledger.json`, the map still records level 2 on nothing measured, and the atom's raw block now measures 11,953 B against the 12,288 B per-atom cap -- 335 B of headroom, and the commit that landed it says plainly that the next pass on it wedges every lane. Of the other two items: EP1 was named FIRST, with the diagnosis settled and told not to re-derive it, was drawn, and `saas/churn_model.py::churn_probability` is byte-identical -- still `min(BASE_ANNUAL_CHURN_PROBABILITY + bill_shock_count * CHURN_UPLIFT_PER_BILL_SHOCK, MAX_CHURN_PROBABILITY)`, the ledger still stamped 2026-08-26T11:46:22Z with `distinct_hazards: 1`, `hazard_histogram {"0.05": 33}` and a believed tenure of 20.0 years for all 33 graded accounts. Third naming, second stretch drawn-and-unchanged. And `python3 -m tools.run_value_cycle_ab` was not run for the third stretch running: the newest artefact is still 17:09:29Z, and none of the four `value_cycle_ab*.json` on the tree contains `gross_to_net_bridge`, `bound_attribution` or `cross_section_reconciliation`. I have to add one thing about my own instrument, because it changes how much of this brief I trusted. The brief handed me `steered: true` and "the previous direction named work the draw then took". That signal is a constant. `direction.focus_was_drawn` reads `.atom_stall_tracker.json`, which is keyed by maturity-map atom id, so a Lane 0 slug can never appear in it -- and the two ids carrying the PASS were EP1, which did not move, and EP13, which moved sideways, while the one item that landed completely was a Lane 0 slug the control cannot represent at all. My own feedback loop credited the two failures and was blind to the success. I read the commits instead and will keep doing that. Against the thesis: the advantage is still unattributed, and this stretch's honest contribution is proving that the measurement everyone was waiting on cannot attribute it at this sample. That is not backwards. It is the most useful negative result the project has produced, and it names its own successor -- a price ladder -- which is why that is now second on this list and why the arm stays off the renewal desk.

R14: every figure carries its clock.
focus.why: Owed for three stretches, about 23 minutes of machine time, no judgement, and it is the only published answer to the question the director actually asked. It describes a book the company stopped having on 26 August. Three instruments were BUILT for this reading and none has ever emitted a number -- `gross_to_net_bridge` (the named decomposition of the GBP 30,924 gap where control gross GBP 433,174.76 fell to arm GBP 419,023.25 while net rose GBP 16,773.28, with `unexplained_residual_gbp` and a reconstruction error so a decomposition that does not close says so), `bound_attribution` and `cross_section_reconciliation`. The residual is the deliverable whatever it is; a bridge that does not close is a finding, not an embarrassment.

focus.what: Build and run the price ladder that the 2026-08-27 section of `docs/design/THE_VALUE_CYCLE_REALISED_AB.md` names as the thing that would separate the two explanations, and publish the two slopes side by side. Concretely: re-run the value arm over the same book and the same seed at several fixed margin multipliers, and compare the SLOPE of realised non-renewals against price with the slope the company's own `company/crm/churn_model.py::estimate_churn_probability` predicts over the same rungs. Fixed rolls are what make this work where the 42-renewal comparison did not -- it needs no matched pairs, so the 18 accounts the world rolled no decision for stop being a hole. Two cheap things travel with it. Publish `rate_vs_svt_pct` beside `rate_increase_pct` per decision, because that section established the company keys on a delta against its own prior rate while the world keys on a level against SVT and both call sites are cited there -- those are different questions and the artefact currently reports only one of them. And either close the 18-unmatched hole or state per account why no decision was rolled. THE OUTPUT IS A MEASUREMENT. If the slopes disagree, the company's belief is the company's own affair and is allowed to be wrong; changing the WORLD's switching response is a baseline fidelity change under R13, must be decided blind to what it does to this delta, and is not this seat's to make -- record it for the curriculum if that is where the arithmetic lands.
focus.why: This is the only remaining route to the director's actual question. The advantage must come from INFERENCE and not from ACCESS; the ceiling reconciliation established last stretch that it must not come from a BOUND either; and this stretch added a fourth way for it to be hollow that nothing has measured -- it can come from PRICE. The realised comparison can no longer settle that, and the verdict it returned was explicitly the third option: the sample cannot separate them, effective n is 4. A ladder measures response to price directly, on a population that cannot dodge it. It is second only because item one is 23 minutes and refreshes the population this would be read against. Finished when two slopes are published beside each other -- realised non-renewal against price, and believed against the same price -- each with the number of decisions behind it, and the section says which of the three verdicts the ladder now supports. If it supports "the win is price, not prediction", say that in the headline where a reader hits it.

focus.what: Fourth naming, and this time a short instruction: MAKE THE CHANGE, do not restate the diagnosis. `company/analytics/clv_three_horizon.py` takes `hazard = latest.churn_probability` at H2 and the term `1.0 / hazard`; that resolves to `saas/churn_model.py::churn_probability`, a step function of one integer that is zero for every graded account, which is why 33 of 33 sit at 0.05 and 20.0 years. The richer sibling already exists and already takes the right arguments: `company/crm/churn_model.py::estimate_churn_probability(old_rate_gbp_per_mwh, new_rate_gbp_per_mwh, tenure_years, annual_consumption_kwh, fuel, hedge_fraction, hangover_periods_remaining, segment, market_move_pct)`. So the work is to feed H2's hazard from per-account observables through that signature rather than to invent a model, widening only where a real supplier could see: payment method and payment behaviour, tenure to date, the account's own rate against the market it could switch to, consumption volatility, contact and complaint history, and whether the account carries a gas leg -- 395 of 397 accounts are residential and the funnel now wins gas legs, so dual-fuel is a live per-account observable. Name every new input with the observable it comes from and clear it against the wall; `company/interfaces/sim_interface.py` is the only door. Then re-measure with `python3 -m tools.couple_clv` and report the ledger's next reading whichever way it moves.
focus.why: "Decisions customer-by-customer on LIFETIME VALUE" and a lifetime term taking exactly one value across the entire graded population are the same claim and its refutation, sitting in one file. The level is not the problem -- `hazard_calibration` shows 0.05 believed against 0.0532 realised over 263 decisions, and 13 distinct believed hazards exist elsewhere in that block, so the estimator CAN take other values and the graded constant is a fact about the input, not the model. This is DISPERSION, and R12 forbids tuning anything toward a smaller gap. It is third rather than first because it has now been ordered second twice and first once and the position is clearly not the variable -- the instruction is, so this one is a quarter the length and names the function to call. Finished when the graded population shows more than one distinct hazard and the ledger's next entry comes from a changed estimator rather than a changed sample. A move to level 3 is available on that evidence if the coupled rung is genuinely met -- self-certify with `record_level_up_self_certified`, never `--no-verify` a `level_current` change. If the gap worsens, that is the result and saying so is the deliverable.

what_next.why_this_is_here: Direction multiplies the draw's existing weights and can never zero one, so it can only ever be ignored -- never obeyed by force. Whether it was actually followed is therefore a measurement, not an assumption.

how_to_read_this: The delivery seat wakes on a timer, reads the last stretch, and writes direction -- never code. What it decides biases which work the ticks draw and can never block any of it. Everything on this page is read from a committed record; nothing here is computed a second time.
